title: Related Services
outcomes: Perform and report agreed-upon procedures engagements.
Apply ethical and reporting practices to related services.

meta.exam_tip: Always say "no assurance" for AUP and compilation answers.

concepts.title: Agreed-upon procedures (SRS 4400)
body: In an agreed-upon procedures engagement, the practitioner carries out audit-type procedures agreed with the entity and any appropriate third parties, and reports factual findings. It is a non-assurance engagement: users assess the procedures and findings themselves.

Terms agreed include nature, purpose, procedures, identified users, use restrictions and report form. Independence is not normally required by the standard unless the terms or law require it; if not independent, this is stated.
The report lists the procedures, findings (including errors and exceptions), states that no audit or review was done and no assurance given, and restricts use to the agreed parties.
concepts.analogy: Do exactly what was agreed and report what you found — no opinion.
concepts.work: A lender may ask for agreed procedures on a borrower's stock statements.

concepts.title: Compilation engagements (SRS 4410)
body: In a compilation engagement, the accountant uses accounting expertise to collect, classify and summarise financial information into statements; no assurance is expressed.
The accountant needs knowledge of the business and the framework, reads the compiled information for obvious misstatements, and obtains management's acknowledgement of responsibility.

If information is incorrect, incomplete or misleading, the accountant asks management for revised information; if refused, considers withdrawing. The report states that the work was a compilation, that no audit or review was performed, and that management is responsible.
concepts.analogy: Compile, read for obvious errors, and say clearly no assurance is given.
concepts.work: A small firm hires an accountant to prepare its year-end statements.

concepts.title: Comparing audits, reviews and related services
body: Audits give reasonable assurance (positive opinion); reviews give limited assurance (negative conclusion); agreed-upon procedures and compilations give no assurance.
Related services rely on agreed scope and management-provided information; their usefulness depends on users understanding the limits.
Choosing the right engagement depends on user needs, cost and the level of comfort required.
concepts.analogy: Assurance falls from reasonable to limited to none.
concepts.work: A bank needing comfort on stock may accept AUP findings rather than a full audit.

concepts.title: Reports and practical issues in related services
body: Engagement letters for related services must spell out that no assurance is expressed and that the engagement cannot be relied on to detect errors, fraud or illegal acts.
Ethical requirements still apply (integrity, objectivity, competence, confidentiality, professional behaviour) even when independence is not required.
Reports should avoid wording that implies assurance, and should not be associated with misleading information.
concepts.analogy: No assurance does not mean no ethics.
concepts.work: An accountant should refuse to compile statements known to be misleading.

illustrations.title: Reporting factual findings
illustrations.q: A franchisor asks the auditor to perform agreed procedures on a franchisee's royalty claim: total sales invoices for the quarter, compare with the sales reported in the royalty statement (₹45 lakh), and recompute royalty at 5%. The invoices total ₹48.6 lakh. What does the report contain?

head: Element
Content
rows: Invoices total ₹48.6 lakh vs reported ₹45 lakh — difference ₹3.6 lakh; royalty underpaid accordingly
No assurance expressed; users draw their own conclusions
Restricted to parties who agreed to the procedures
solution.title: SRS 4400 report

checks.label: Difference found between invoices and claim (₹ lakh)

illustrations.title: Compilation with known errors
illustrations.q: During a compilation for Nova Traders, the accountant notices that depreciation has not been charged and opening balances seem wrong. Management refuses to correct them. What should the accountant do?

head: Step
Action
rows: Bring the matters to management's attention and propose corrections
Consider withdrawing from the engagement; otherwise ensure the statements are not misleading
No duty to verify all balances — but do not ignore known errors
States that no audit or review was performed and no assurance is given
solution.title: SRS 4410

jobs.title: AUP for a lender
jobs.situation: A bank wants factual findings on a borrower's receivable ageing.
steps: Agree procedures with bank and borrower.
Restrict the report to the bank and borrower.
jobs.takeaway: Clear terms and factual reporting protect everyone.

mcqs.explain: Factual findings only. In practice: users conclude.

remember: Audit: reasonable; review: limited; related: none.
traps: Expressing an opinion in an AUP report.

viva.q: What is the objective of an AUP engagement?
viva.model: To perform procedures of an audit nature agreed with the entity and users and report factual findings.
Using accounting expertise to collect, classify and summarise financial information, where the accountant gives users zero assurance.
Audits give reasonable assurance, reviews limited assurance, and related services give none.
Because people unaware of the reasons for the procedures may misread the findings.

viva.q: Which ethical principles apply to related services?
viva.model: Integrity, objectivity, confidentiality, professional behaviour, and competence exercised with due care.

cases.title: Harmony Foods
cases.case: Harmony Foods engages a CA to compile its statements for internal use. Opening balances contain errors. A team member suggests verifying all balances like an audit. The client also wants the CA to perform agreed procedures for its distributor on rebate claims.

mcqs.q: Verifying all balances in the compilation is:
options: Not required, but known errors must be addressed
mcqs.explain: Compilation is not an audit. In practice: read for obvious errors.

mcqs.q: The opening balance errors should be:
options: Brought to management's attention for correction
mcqs.explain: SRS 4410. In practice: withdraw if refused.

mcqs.q: The rebate claims work is governed by:
mcqs.explain: Agreed-upon procedures. In practice: factual findings.

mcqs.q: The AUP report should be restricted to:
mcqs.explain: Agreeing parties. In practice: state clearly.
